description:
FILED s410 (Opus 5) as the measured residue of #342 piece 2.

t/base/lex.t mixes the "heredoc opened inside an interpolation block inside an
s///e replacement" construct FIVE ways (lines 292-326).  #342 piece 2 (s410)
fixed the one where the heredoc BODY sits inside the s/// delimiters, because
there the replacement text PCL is handed already contains it:

    s|(?:)|"${\<<END}"
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in multiline s///e outside eval
    END
    |e;                                     <- FIXED s410, matches perl

The other four put the body AFTER the statement, so the replacement text is
only `"${\<<END}"` and the body lives in the enclosing DOCUMENT:

    eval ' s/(?:)/"${\<<END}"/e;
    ok $test - heredoc in "" in single-line s///e in eval
    END
    ';
      perl: ok 4 - heredoc …
      PCL : $@ = "The function main::pl-END is undefined"   (LOUD, trappable)

plus the `. <<\END` variant, the multiline-in-eval variant, and the
`<<foo` + NUL-on-the-same-line variant.  All four are inside `eval '...'`, so
the failure is a trappable $@, never a wrong value.

WHY IT IS SEPARATE: the s///e replacement compiler is handed a STRING.  The
piece-2 pre-pass (`Pl::ExprToCL::_splice_interp_heredocs`) can hoist a body it
can SEE; these four need the body pulled from the enclosing document, where
PPI has already lexed those lines as ordinary statements (it never saw the
opener, because the opener is inside a Quote::Double token).  That is a
DOCUMENT-level pre-pass: find a heredoc opener inside a string, take the
following lines up to the terminator, attach them to the token, and REMOVE
those statements from the document.  It is the same shape as the existing
`_ppi_parse` repair chain, so that is where it belongs — but it touches every
document, not just a replacement that already failed, so it needs the
full emission verification, not a retry.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR t/base/lex.t: that file still fails to transpile on a
DIFFERENT construct two lines later —

    s/${s|||;\""}not //;        PCL: cannot compile interpolated regex
                                     reference '${s|||;\""}'

a `s///` inside an interpolation block inside a s/// PATTERN.  So no row moves
until both are done, which is why #342's own note said "do NOT size the file's
120 rows against piece 2 alone".

POPULATION: t/base/lex.t only, in both populations (grepped s410).

Related: #342 (both pieces), #363 (an eval-mode drop dies into $@ — which is
why these four are loud).
subject: A heredoc opened inside an interpolation block whose BODY is outside the s/// delimiters needs a DOCUMENT-level pre-pass (4 of base/lex.t's 5 shapes; loud in $@ today) — #342 piece 2 fixed only the in-delimiters one
